events.what: Iran's Araghchi says talks with US via Qatari mediators on reopening Hormuz are ongoing; Iran demands US lift maritime blockade, ease sanctions, release frozen assets; Rubio says any acceptable deal is up to the US President
Brent briefly fell below $107/b on talk of Qatar-Pakistan peace initiative, then rebounded after Iran's president said Tehran would not negotiate until US accepts its conditions
Tanker struck by unknown projectile 30 nautical miles off Al Faw, Iraq (UKMTO), no reported damage
Aframax crude tanker hit 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman, and caught fire (Vanguard TECH)
IRGC says two oil tankers on the 'unauthorized' route nearer Oman hit mines and caught fire; Iranian state TV reports a tanker set ablaze in Hormuz southern corridor
Iran says it opened 'special routes' for Iraqi ships through Hormuz
Hormuz transits fell for a third day to 16 ships; no VLCCs on Oct. 19; none detected on a day for first time since Aug. 2 (per Oct. 20 CAS data)
Houthis declared maritime blockade on Saudi-linked shipping at Bab al-Mandab; Saudi crude rerouted via Suez/SUMED
US Treasury (OFAC) sanctions Panama/Greece law firm, shell companies and vessels tied to Iranian oil, LPG and petrochemicals trade
First Russian diesel tanker (40,000 mt) to US since Jan 2022 set to leave Baltic after US sanctions waiver; Russia targets 300,000 mt for US in Oct and 500,000 mt in Nov
Putin tells US envoy Witkoff prices fell 5-6% on the international market after announcement of new exports to the US
Rubio says India could import more Venezuelan heavy crude and invest upstream in Venezuela
Hurricane Isaias made landfall as Cat 2 near Destin, Florida; peak GoM crude shut-in about 1.459 million b/d
ExxonMobil 267,000 b/d Joliet refinery reports ongoing flaring from unit upset, second filing of week
PetroChina Dalian Petrochemical to restart without Russian ESPO crude; 200,000 b/d CDU targeted end-November at earliest
UK approves Jackdaw gas development and launches GBP 2 billion Energy Wealth Fund
DOE offers loan of up to 315,000 barrels from Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve; IEA members plan release of over 20 million barrels of diesel
Seoul rejects refiners' request to ease cap on product exports (capped at 2025 levels)
Japan to provide kerosene import subsidies from Oct. 21 to March 20, 2027; fuel subsidy cut to 42.80 yen/liter for Oct. 22-28
KPC says talks with Gulf allies on pipelines to move crude are progressing, engineering phases under way
Enbridge Mainline apportionment at 16% heavy for November; WCS discounts at multi-year wides

themes.theme: Hormuz disruption and attacks on tankers
themes.summary: Hormuz transits fell for a third day to 16 ships with no VLCCs on Oct. 19, tankers were hit near Al Faw and Bukha, and Iraq's loadings slowed to 690,900 b/d in the last 10 days from about 3.06 million b/d in the first 10 days of October.

Iran says talks via Qatari mediators continue but sets conditions the US has largely opposed, and Brent briefly dipped below $107/b on Oct. 20 before recovering on Iran's refusal to negotiate until conditions are accepted.

themes.theme: Saudi rerouting to Red Sea, Suez and SUMED amid Houthi blockade
themes.summary: Suez tanker transits reached 143 in the week ended Oct. 15, Saudi northbound crude via Suez reached about 653,000 b/d in Oct. 1-19, and VLCC freight from Yanbu and Sidi Kerir to the Far East set records.

themes.theme: US crude inventory draws and Hurricane Isaias shut-ins
themes.summary: US commercial crude fell 3.06 million barrels to 412.52 million with SPR at a 44-year low of 282.68 million, though Cushing rose for a fifth week and US output fell 3% to 13.27 million b/d.

themes.theme: Record-high product cracks and diesel tightness
themes.summary: Singapore gasoil crack was $66.91/b on Oct. 20 after a record $83.02/b on Sept. 16, ICE gasoil settled at $1,449.5/mt on Oct. 20, and Russia plans small diesel shipments to the US under a sanctions waiver.

themes.theme: Weak freight-hit regional crude differentials (WAF, WCS, CPC, Med)
themes.summary: WCS Hardisty traded at a $28.00/b discount to WTI CMA, CPC Blend CFR Augusta was offered at a $6.25/b discount to Dated Brent, and West African differentials remain pressured by low Chinese buying and high freight.

themes.theme: Middle East sour strength and record-low East-West spreads
themes.summary: Cash Dubai and Oman rose to $5.54/b premiums to Dubai futures and the December Brent-Dubai swap spread hit minus $2.38/b, a record low since 2001.

themes.theme: Latin American and Venezuelan supply growth
themes.summary: Venezuela output is near 1.2 million b/d with Weatherford and Halliburton ramping up, India Venezuelan crude inflows are rising, and Argentina exports rose to 9.9 million barrels in September.
